programme: No single programme unifies these eleven factors. They fall into at least three unrelated functional classes: Müllerian/endometrial epithelial identity and oncogenic drivers (SOX17, ARID1A, HOXA1, E2F8), a neuronal gene-repression and dopaminergic axis (REST, NR4A2), and a residual set with no defined joint function or disease link (GLIS3, GTF3A, DMTF1, TFAP4, HMBOX1). RARA is discordant and does not belong to the concordant set at all. None of these factors are known to physically complex, share a target module, or sit in one documented pathway together.
role_in_a: In Endometrioid_Cancer, SOX17 and ARID1A are established diagnostic/tumor-suppressor markers of Müllerian carcinomas, HOXA1 has a described oncogenic axis (HOTAIRM1/HOXA1) in endometrial cancer, and E2F8 is a cell-cycle driver — but these act as separate, individually documented factors, not as one programme.
role_in_b: In Stroke, REST is a well-known ischemia-induced neuronal gene repressor and NR4A2 (Nurr1) has documented neuroprotective and vascular-injury roles; HOXA1 loss-of-function causes cerebrovascular (carotid) malformation that predisposes to stroke. Again these are independent facts about separate genes, not a shared circuit.
shared_axis: No shared mechanism is supported by the record. The closest candidate — HOXA1 and SOX17 both having secondary roles in vascular/arterial specification alongside their epithelial roles — is not established by any retrieved paper for this pair; it would have to be asserted from general embryology, not from what was retrieved.
reasoning: The concordant set spans oncogenic epithelial markers, a neuronal repressor, a nuclear receptor, general transcription/cell-cycle factors, and several genes with zero literature or Open Targets signal in either disease; there is no complex or pathway that plausibly carries all or most of them. Given the explicit instruction not to force a story onto factors that merely co-occur, and that most retrieved papers are noted as off-topic for the query that produced them, this pair does not clear the bar for a mechanistic account.
support: PMID 42162929, 41510478, 42274628 — ARID1A is a documented SWI/SNF tumor suppressor in endometrioid/endometrial carcinoma, but only as an individual gene fact, not part of a cross-disease module. PMID 31853186 — HOXA1 (via HOTAIRM1) drives endometrial cancer cell proliferation/invasion, an isolated gene-disease link. PMID 39541495, 37508332 — HOXA1-related disorders and hoxa1a-null zebrafish show HOXA1 loss causes cerebrovascular/cardiac malformation, again an isolated developmental fact unconnected to the endometrial finding by any retrieved source. PMID 41419029, 42237586 — NR4A2 is implicated in neurological and ischemic-stroke mechanisms, with no bearing on endometrioid cancer. PMID 42669756 — REST is mentioned only incidentally alongside a cortical stroke case report and does not establish a REST-stroke mechanism.
how_to_falsify: Test whether the concordant factors actually co-regulate a shared target set: take ChIP-seq/ReMap or ATAC data from matched endometrial and vascular/neuronal cell types and check whether SOX17, HOXA1, ARID1A, REST, and NR4A2 co-occupy the same promoters/enhancers. If their target sets are non-overlapping and each factor's perturbation produces a transcriptional signature specific to only one tissue with no cross-tissue enrichment, that confirms there is no shared programme; conversely, significant co-binding or a shared downstream signature across both tissue types would overturn the incoherent call.
caveats: The tissue pairing itself (blood-derived stroke signal vs. uterine endometrium tissue) is biologically distant, and most factors carry no Open Targets association with either disease. Several concordant factors (GTF3A, DMTF1, GLIS3) have no literature hits for either disease at all, and RARA — a nuclear receptor that might otherwise link retinoic-acid signaling across both tissues — was discordant and excluded. The tissue-generic exclusion list already removed likely broad immune/stress regulators (STAT1, SPI1, MEF2C, BCL6, CEBPD, IRF1), so what remains is not simply masked generic signal, but it is also not a coherent residual module — it looks more consistent with independent, tissue-specific regulators recurring by chance across 36 patient-group comparisons than with one shared axis.
